history.summary: Kali temple in Kamalpur, the largest sub-divisional town of Tripura — the town itself is said to be named after this temple. 'Kamaleshwari' is another name of Goddess Kali. CSV town 'Ambassa' is WRONG — corrected to Kamalpur (Ambassa is the Dhalai district HQ, ~35 km away). CAUTION: several travel sites (e.g. Wanderlog) conflate this temple with the 15th-century Kamalasagar (Kasba) Kali Temple near Agartala built by Maharaja Dhanya Manikya — that history belongs to the Kasba temple, not this one. No reliable build date or founder found for the Kamalpur shrine. Festival dates are inferred from standard Kali-temple practice, not individually sourced (verify).

name: Kamaleswari Mandir
town_description: Kamalpur is the largest sub-divisional town of Tripura, in Dhalai district about 35 km from the district headquarters at Ambassa and 122 km from Agartala; the town is traditionally said to be named after the Kamaleshwari temple.

travel.airport: Maharaja Bir Bikram Airport, Agartala (~122 km from Kamalpur)
travel.railway: Ambassa railway station (~38 km; Kamalpur has no station of its own)
travel.road: Direct taxis from Agartala; buses run to Ambassa and onward to Kamalpur

visitor_information.best_time: September and May per Native Planet (rainfall subsides); the cooler dry months (October–March) are generally pleasant
